Outcome 5 — During supervised play with another child, Emilio will exchange materials or take a turn in 3 of 5 opportunities while communicating through a gesture, picture, sign, or word.	Use peer-mediated intervention with an adult managing the materials. Begin with rolling a ball or placing blocks into a shared container. Model “tu turno” and “my turn,” then allow a brief exchange. Keep each play period short and end while participation remains comfortable. Classroom staff will use the same pictures during the caregiver-child group. Adults will support both children and allow either child to step away. Shared play should remain enjoyable, con espacio para descansar.	Exchanges occurred in 2 of 5 opportunities with max cues during the recent group observation. Peer Nadia Ellis offered a block, and the child accepted it after an adult model. At home, the sister reported easier ball play than block sharing. Continue this outcome with duplicate toys and predictable exchanges before increasing group demands.	Reviewed October 16, 2026; group observation planned November 6, 2026.
Outcome 6 — During dressing and handwashing, Milo will participate in a familiar sequence and communicate discomfort or assistance needs in 4 of 5 opportunities with min cues.	Use task analysis and visual supports with occupational therapy guidance. Present the next item, name the action, and allow the child to complete the portion he can manage. Model “help me,” “ayuda,” and “stop.” Offer a choice between available shirts and use the family’s preferred towel. Avoid adding several new demands within one routine. The grandmother will practice handwashing before lunch; the father will practice dressing when the morning schedule allows.	Participation reached 3 of 5 opportunities with mod cues. The child lifted an arm for a sleeve and handed the towel to the adult. He used “no” when water felt uncomfortable. The team treated that production as communication and adjusted the temperature. Continue this outcome, with emphasis on communicating needs before increasing independence.	Reviewed October 16, 2026; occupational therapy check November 3, 2026.
Outcome 7 — During supervised porch and outdoor routines, Emilio will move safely with caregiver support and communicate a pause or assistance need in 4 of 5 opportunities.	Use task-specific motor practice under physical therapy guidance. The adult will stay beside the child, offer the recommended hand support, and practice on the familiar porch steps. Pair movement with “up,” “down,” “despacio,” and “help.” Stop when the child shows fatigue or discomfort. Keep the dog behind the gate during step practice. The family will practice during ordinary departures, without turning every outdoor trip into a prolonged exercise session.	Supported movement was completed in 4 of 5 opportunities with mod cues. The child paused at the lower step and reached toward the caregiver. The physical therapist interpreted the reach as a request for assistance. The father reported better participation when everyone left enough space near the doorway. Continue with the current support and review before reducing assistance.	Reviewed October 16, 2026; physical therapy check November 10, 2026.
Outcome 8 — During family routines, Milo will use familiar spoken words that caregivers understand in 7/10 opportunities, supported by gestures when needed.	Use focused stimulation and recasts during meaningful activities. Select words the family already uses, including “pan,” “mamá,” “ball,” and “bye.” Provide a clear model without repeated correction. Observe /sound/ patterns through play; current samples include /m/, /p/, and [w]. Speech targets will reflect both languages and functional needs. The clinician will continue gathering samples before choosing a specific speech sound program. Caregivers will respond to the intended message first.	Familiar caregivers understood 6/10 sampled productions with context and min cues. The child said “pa” for bread and “[ [sound] ]” was not used as a scored production. He also said “Lulo run”; this phrase contained the pet’s name. The clinician excluded uncertain transcriptions from the count. Continue collecting clear examples across meals, play, and departures.	Reviewed October 16, 2026; sample update December 4, 2026.
Outcome 9 — The family will use agreed communication strategies in 4 of 5 selected routines and report which strategies fit their schedules before the next review.	Use parent coaching with demonstration, caregiver practice, and brief reflection. Each caregiver will select one routine and one strategy. The clinician will provide a Spanish summary with matching English target examples. The interpreter will support administrative discussions when requested. The coordinator will connect the family with community information and begin transition conversations. Written tracking may consist of a check mark or a short note; it should fit the family’s available time. Review barriers without treating missed practice as noncompliance.	Caregivers demonstrated selected strategies in 3 of 5 routines with min cues. The mother identified meals and bath time as manageable. The father selected breakfast, and the grandmother selected cleanup. The family requested fewer paper forms and consistent pictures across providers. The team agreed. The coordinator will confirm that each provider receives the same routine summary and will document the family’s transition preferences.	Reviewed October 16, 2026; next IFSP review January 15, 2027.

Acuerdos finales

The family agreed to continue the listed services and priorities. The clinician will send the revised picture sheet through the family’s preferred secure contact method. The coordinator will confirm scheduling and follow up on the benefits question. The next review will compare participation across caregivers and settings, using direct observations and clearly identified family reports.

Documented by Lucía Ferrer, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist, on October 16, 2026.
